newsitem.title: USA: Fannie Oct mortgage portfolio grew $1.5 bln.
newsitem.headline: Fannie Oct mortgage portfolio grew $1.5 bln.

text.p: The Federal National Mortgage Association said Wednesday its net mortgage portfolio grew by $1.5 billion in October to $278.5 billion.
The annualized growth rate was 6.6 percent, slower than 12.3 percent in September, Fannie Mae's monthly summary said.

Mortgage purchases were $4.2 billion in October, compared with $5.4 billion in September, while portfolio liquidations were $2.6 billion in October, compared with $2.5 billion in September, Fannie Mae said.
Net commitments to purchase mortgages rose to $5.2 billion in October, up from $4.2 billion in September, Fannie Mae said.

The conventional single-family serious delinquency rate was 0.56 percent in September compared with 0.55 percent in August, Fannie Mae said. The conventional multifamily at-risk serious delinquency rate rose to 0.91 percent in September from 0.84 percent in August, Fannie Mae said.
Total mortgage-backed securities outstanding rose by $4.9 billion in October to $641.3 billion, a 9.2 percent annualized growth rate, Fannie Mae said.
Mortgage-backed securities outstanding net of securities held in portfolio increased by $3.1 billion in October to $546.7 billion, a 6.8 percent annualized rate.

Fannie Mae's net interest margin on the mortgage portfolio was 131 basis points in October, unchanged from September. The overall net interest margin was 117 basis points in October, down one basis point from September, Fannie Mae said.
